docs.title: GTM Validator: The Big Picture
docs.text: Project Mission: To provide startups with a "Data-Driven Second Opinion" on their Go-To-Market strategy, bridging the gap between qualitative maturity and quantitative growth.

docs.title: 🌟 The Core Value Proposition
docs.text:
The GTM Validator isn't just a survey tool; it's a Maturity Operating System. It solves the three most common problems for scaling companies:

  1. Blind Spots: Identifying exactly where execution is failing (e.g., "We have leads, but our Win Rate is low").
  2. Strategic Paralysis: Removing the "What now?" by using AI to write a specific, actionable 30-day playbook.
  3. Proof Gap: Validating that your "Best-in-Class" claims match the reality of your sales decks and landing pages.

docs.title: 🛠️ The Tech Stack Vision
docs.text:
We chose a "Modern Monolith" architecture to ensure maximum speed of delivery and zero friction between the AI and the Database.

  • The Brain (Django 5.2.7): Handles the complex weighted scoring and multi-tenant security.
  • The Eyes (Google Vertex AI / Gemini): Performs multimodal audits of images and PDFs.
  • The Interaction (HTMX & Tailwind): Provides a seamless, "Single Page App" experience without the overhead of a heavy JS framework.
  • The Memory (PostgreSQL & Redis Cache): Ensures results are snapshotted and AI responses are throttled for reliability.

docs.title: 🚀 Key Innovation: The "Vision-to-Scoring" Bridge
docs.text: One of the project's unique architectural features is the Automated Auditor. In most platforms, the user self-reports their score. In GTM Validator, the user uploads their Strategic Evidence, and the AI Auditor calculates a Score Modifier (-3 to +3) that adjusts their maturity rating based on actual asset quality.

docs.title: 🗺️ Documentation Roadmap
docs.text:
This documentation is designed to serve as a Single Source of Truth for three distinct audiences:

  • Business Leaders: Use the Plain English Guide to understand the ROI and product vision.
  • Senior Developers: Use the Developer Deep Dive and Core Logic to understand the weighted math and AI orchestration.
  • DevOps & Infrastructure: Use the Management Tools and Data Models to understand environment setup and data persistence.

The GTM Validator is built to turn business uncertainty into strategic momentum.

docs.title: Intelligence & AI Engine: Technical Reference
docs.text:
The Big Picture

The AI Engine is the GTM Validator's "Executive Consultant." It doesn't just generate text; it observes the database state, audits visual files, and mutates the task backlog. The architecture is built for resilience, ensuring that even if Gemini is down, the user still receives high-quality pre-written guidance.

docs.title: 1. Interaction Layer (gtm/ai_services.py)
docs.text: The system interacts with Vertex AI via the google-genai SDK. The core entry point is generate_playbook_with_gemini.

docs.title: Prompt Orchestration
docs.text:
Prompts are not static strings; they are dynamically constructed using data from the ResultSnapshot.

# gtm/ai_services.py
def _build_playbook_prompt(snapshot):
    category_data = snapshot.category_breakdown
    weak_answers = Response.objects.filter(session=snapshot.session, score__lte=2)

    # The prompt forces a specific JSON structure for easy parsing
    return f"""
    Analyze this GTM data for {snapshot.company_name} ({snapshot.industry}):
    Overall Score: {snapshot.overall}
    Categories: {json.dumps(category_data)}
    Weak Points: {[r.question.text for r in weak_answers]}

    Return a JSON object with: 
    - "markdown_playbook": A 30-day strategy.
    - "financial_summary": Estimated ROI.
    - "competitor_analysis": Gap assessment.
    """

docs.title: Safety & Quota Logic
docs.text:
To handle enterprise-grade stability, the engine implements a global Quota Cooldown.

# gtm/ai_services.py
def _set_quota_cooldown():
    # If Vertex AI returns 'ResourceExhausted', we pause for 5 minutes
    cache.set("gtm:ai:quota_cooldown", True, timeout=300)

def generate_playbook_with_gemini(snapshot):
    if cache.get("gtm:ai:quota_cooldown"):
        # Revert to safe pre-written content
        return _fallback_to_static_content(snapshot)

docs.title: 2. Multimodal Auditor (gtm/ai_auditor.py)
docs.text: The auditor handles visual strategic evidence. It supports Image (Landing Pages) and PDF (Sales Decks).

docs.title: Binary Data Flow
docs.text:
Files are never sent as URLs; they are sent as raw binary parts to ensure the AI "sees" the exact state of the asset.

# gtm/ai_auditor.py
def audit_gtm_file(gtm_file_id):
    file_obj = GTMFile.objects.get(id=gtm_file_id)
    with file_obj.file.open('rb') as f:
        content = f.read()

    # Multimodal call sending text prompt + image bytes
    response = client.models.generate_content(
        model='gemini-2.5-flash',
        contents=[
            types.Part.from_text("Critique this landing page for GTM clarity."),
            types.Part.from_bytes(data=content, mime_type="image/png")
        ]
    )

docs.title: 3. Agentic Autonomy (gtm/ai_chat.py)
docs.text: The chat assistant is an Agent, meaning it can take actions in the database.

docs.title: Intent Detection
docs.text: The AI doesn't just talk; it classifies the user's "Intent."

docs.title:
# gtm/ai_chat.py
# If user says "Make a task for that," the intent 'execution_plan' is triggered.
if intent == 'execution_plan':
    # This Python function creates ActionItem rows in the DB automatically
    return build_execution_plan(session, ai_recommendations)
docs.text: Technical Note: All AI interactions are logged to AIUsageTracker for cost and performance monitoring.

docs.title: Developer Reference: API & Views
docs.text: The GTM Validator uses a mix of standard Django views and HTMX-powered partials to manage the assessment lifecycle and AI interactions.

docs.title: 1. The Assessment Wizard (gtm/views.py)
docs.text: The assessment process is managed through a single-view, multi-step pattern: - assessment_step: This view dynamically renders questions based on the current_step of the AssessmentSession. - HTMX Integration: If a request contains the HX-Request header, the view returns only the form partial. This prevents full page reloads and maintains the "Single Page App" feel of the diagnostic. - State Management: Scores and context notes are saved to Response objects on every "Next" click, ensuring zero data loss if a user disconnects.

docs.title: 2. Asynchronous AI Polling
docs.text: Because playbook generation and diagnostic insights are non-blocking (running in background threads), the frontend uses polling to update the UI. - playbook_status View: Returns the ai_playbook_status of a ResultSnapshot. Once "done", it triggers an HTMX swap to display the final playbook. - insight_status View: Similar logic for individual question-level diagnostics.

docs.title: 3. Real-Time Context Optimization
docs.text: The rewrite_context_note view provides an "AI Assist" for user notes: - Endpoint: Post a note to this view, and it returns a "cleaned" version using ai_services.rewrite_context_note_with_ai. - UI: This is used in the assessment form to help users turn raw thoughts into specific, actionable business context that improves the final AI playbook.

docs.title: 4. Multimodal Audit Endpoints
docs.text: The asset library uses specialized views to trigger and track audits: - trigger_resource_audit: Spawns an audit_resource_async thread for a specific Resource. - HTMX Trigger: When a file is uploaded, an HTMX trigger calls the audit endpoint automatically, showing a "Critiquing..." spinner in the UI until the AI Auditor finishes its vision analysis.

docs.title: 5. Report Generation (utils_pdf.py)
docs.text: The download_report view handles the generation of the professional PDF report: - Dynamic Context: It aggregates data from the ResultSnapshot, Category scores, and the AI Playbook. - Binary Stream: It returns a FileResponse containing the generated ReportLab PDF, allowing for direct download or browser viewing.

docs.title: Technical Substace & Core Logic
docs.text: This document explains the technical "Why" behind the GTM Validator. It bridges the gap between the product features and the Django/AI implementation.

docs.title: 1. Weighted Scoring Architecture
docs.text:
The "Substance" of the GTM assessment relies on a hierarchical weighting system. Not all questions are equal.

  • Question Weights: Found in gtm/models.py. A question like "Do you have a documented ICP?" is weighted higher (1.25) than "Do you capture proof points?" (0.95).
  • Normalization: In gtm/services.py, category scores are normalized to a 100-point scale. This ensures that even if one category has 10 questions and another has 5, they impact the final "Maturity Rating" according to the business-defined importance (Demand: 40%, Conversion: 40%, Delivery: 20%).

docs.title: 2. The "Vision-to-Value" Bridge
docs.text:
The project includes a unique integration between visual auditing and numerical scoring (gtm/ai_auditor.py).

  • Logic: The AI Auditor doesn't just provide text feedback. It returns an "Evidence Score" (1-10).
  • Implementation: The code uses a regex-based parser (_extract_score_modifier) to turn LLM prose into a numeric integer (-3 to +3).
  • Business Impact: This modifier is applied to the ResultSnapshot, meaning a company's GTM maturity rating is validated by actual evidence, not just their self-reported answers.

docs.title: 3. Resilient AI Pipeline
docs.text:
AI is unpredictable. The GTM Validator uses several patterns to ensure the platform stays "Up" even when the AI is "Down" or slow.

  • Background Processing: Tasks like playbook generation are handled in background threads (threading.Thread). The user sees a "Generating..." status while the AI works, and the UI polls for completion using HTMX.
  • JSON Sanitization: LLMs often break JSON formatting. gtm/ai_services.py includes a _clean_json_response utility that "rescues" the content by stripping markdown tags and finding structural JSON boundaries.
  • Static Fallbacks: If the Gemini API hits a quota limit or fails, the platform automatically switches to "Safe Mode," serving high-quality pre-written advice from the RecommendationBand models.

docs.title: 4. Multi-Tenant Data Isolation
docs.text:
The "Workspace" feature uses a Soft Isolation model (gtm/models_workspace.py).

  • Pattern: Every major data point (AssessmentSession, ActionItem, Resource) has an optional workspace foreign key.
  • Authorization: Permission checks are centralized in safe_get_session_or_403. This ensures that "Contributor" A in "Workspace" X can never see data from "Workspace" Y, while still allowing the same user to have private personal assessments.

docs.title: 5. Document "Eyes" for the Agent
docs.text:
The chat agent can "read" files (dashboard/document_processors.py).

  • OCR Strategy: It uses a hybrid approach. It first tries to parse PDFs locally. If that fails (e.g., a scanned image PDF), it sends the document to Gemini for AI-powered text extraction.
  • Context Windowing: To avoid crashing the AI with too much text, the code tokenizes documents and only sends the most relevant snippets based on the user's specific question.

docs.title: Data Models: Relational Schema & State Management
docs.text:
The Big Picture

The data model is built for Historical Accuracy and Multi-Tenancy. We use the "Snapshot Pattern" to ensure that once an assessment is completed, the results are frozen. This prevents a company's historical report from changing if you later update the diagnostic questions in the Django Admin.

docs.title: 1. Core Relationship Diagram
docs.text:
The assessment engine relies on a hierarchical structure:

  • Category: The high-level GTM pillars (Demand, Conversion, Delivery).
  • Question: The diagnostic units. Each carries ai_metadata for LLM context.
  • AssessmentSession: The container for a single company's checkup.
  • Response: The bridge between a session and a question, storing the 1-5 score.

docs.title: Critical Model: ResultSnapshot
docs.text:
The ResultSnapshot is a one-to-one record with an AssessmentSession. It acts as the "Frozen State" of a completed assessment.

class ResultSnapshot(models.Model):
    session = models.OneToOneField("AssessmentSession", on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    overall = models.FloatField() # Weighted total
    category_breakdown = models.JSONField() # Cached radar chart data
    ai_playbook = models.TextField() # The final Gemini strategy
    report_sent = models.BooleanField(default=False)

docs.title: 2. Workspace & RBAC Architecture
docs.text:
The platform uses a "Soft Tenant" model for collaboration.

  • Workspace: The top-level organization container.
  • WorkspaceMembership: Links a User to a Workspace with a role.
  • Roles: admin, manager, contributor, viewer, funti3r_consultant.

docs.title: Permission Scoping
docs.text:
Permissions are not hardcoded in views. They are enforced via the safe_get_session_or_403 service.

# gtm/services.py
def safe_get_session_or_403(request, session_id):
    session = AssessmentSession.objects.get(uuid=session_id)
    # 1. User owns it personally
    if session.user == request.user: return session
    # 2. User is part of the workspace that owns it
    if request.user in session.workspace.active_members: return session
    # 3. Deny access
    raise PermissionDenied

docs.title: 3. Collaboration & Action Models
docs.text:
The "Execution" phase of the GTM lifecycle is managed by task models:

  • ActionItem: A specific task (e.g., "Refine ICP").
  • ActionItemComment: Threaded team communication.
  • GTMFile: Binary strategic evidence with AI audit metadata.

docs.title: The "Vision Bridge" in Models
docs.text: The GTMFile model includes fields that store AI-calculated modifiers.

docs.title:
class GTMFile(models.Model):
    # stores "Evidence Score: 8/10"
    ai_audit_notes = models.TextField()
    # stores +2 (added to GTM score)
    ai_audit_score_modifier = models.IntegerField(default=0)
docs.text: Technical Note: Use python manage.py load_gtm_defaults to seed the Categories and Questions.

docs.title: Developer Deep Dive: System Architecture & Core Logic
docs.text: This document provides a high-substance technical reference for the GTM Validator. It explains how the system is architected, what each file is responsible for, and dives into the complex logic with actual code references.

docs.title: 1. System Design: The Data Flow
docs.text:
The GTM Validator follows a Diagnostic-to-Action lifecycle. Here is how data moves through the system:

  1. Identity: Middleware ensures every visitor has a gtm_client UUID cookie.
  2. Assessment: AssessmentSession collects responses (1-5 scores + text notes).
  3. Aggregation: gtm.services._compute_scores runs a weighted algorithm to generate a maturity rating.
  4. Snapshotted State: Results are frozen into a ResultSnapshot to prevent recalculation lag.
  5. AI Strategy: Background threads kickoff Gemini to write a 30-day playbook based on the snapshot.
  6. Collaborative Execution: Workspace members turn playbook recommendations into ActionItems.

docs.title: gtm/ (Core Assessment Engine)
docs.text:
• models.py: The "Relational Bible." Defines Categories, Questions, Responses, and the critical ResultSnapshot.
  • services.py: The "Brain." Contains the math for weighted scoring and the logic for safe session retrieval.
  • ai_services.py: The "AI Gateway." Handles interaction with Vertex AI, prompt building, and response sanitization.
  • ai_auditor.py: The "Vision Bridge." Multimodal logic that audits images/PDFs and modifiers the GTM score.
  • views.py: The "Traffic Controller." Manages the multi-step HTMX assessment wizard.
  • middleware.py: Handles anonymous user tracking and persistent identity.

docs.title: dashboard/ (Analytics & Assets)
docs.text:
• analytics.py: Logic for calculating KPI velocity, weekly trends, and workspace-scoped context.
  • document_processors.py: The "Parser." Hybrid PDF/Image OCR engine using local libraries and AI fallback.
  • views.py: Manages the Kanban task board, asset library, and KPI gap reporting.

docs.title: A. The Weighted Scoring Algorithm
docs.text:
The maturity score isn't a simple average. It uses two tiers of weights defined in the load_gtm_defaults command.

# gtm/services.py (simplified logic)
def _compute_scores(session):
    # Tier 1: Question weights (e.g. ICP is 1.25, Testimonials are 0.95)
    category_avg = sum(score * question_weight) / sum(question_weights)

    # Tier 2: Category weights (Demand 40%, Conversion 40%, Delivery 20%)
    overall_score = sum((category_avg / 5) * (cat_weight / total_weight) * 100)
    return overall_score

docs.title: B. Resilient AI: The "Rescue" Pattern
docs.text:
Vertex AI sometimes returns malformed JSON or markdown-wrapped strings. The project uses a regex-based discovery engine to "rescue" the content.

# gtm/ai_services.py
def _normalize_ai_playbook_markdown(playbook_text):
    # Regex fallback: extract content of "markdown_playbook" key if json.loads fails
    match = re.search(r'["\']markdown_playbook["\']\s*:\s*["\'](.*?)(?:["\']\s*,\s*["\']|["\']\s*}|$)', 
                      src, re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        src = match.group(1)

    # Clean up LLM artifacts (\n, \", etc)
    return src.replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\"', '"').strip()

docs.title: C. Multimodal Vision-to-Scoring Bridge
docs.text:
The ai_auditor turns qualitative critiques into quantitative score modifiers.

# gtm/ai_auditor.py
def _extract_score_modifier(audit_text):
    # Regex looks for "Evidence Score: N/10" in the AI's prose
    match = re.search(r"evidence\s+score[:\s*]+(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:/\s*10)?", audit_text, re.I)
    if match:
        score = float(match.group(1))
        # Map 1-10 scale to -3 to +3 GTM score modifier
        if score <= 3: return -3
        if score >= 7: return 3
        return 0

docs.title: D. Multi-Tenant Isolation
docs.text:
Security is enforced by scoping every query to a Workspace while maintaining a fallback for personal assessments.

# dashboard/analytics.py
def get_dashboard_context(request, current_workspace, ...):
    if current_workspace:
        # Strict workspace isolation
        assessments_qs = AssessmentSession.objects.filter(workspace=current_workspace)
        action_items_qs = ActionItem.objects.filter(workspace=current_workspace)
    else:
        # Fallback to private user data
        assessments_qs = AssessmentSession.objects.filter(user=request.user)

docs.title: 4. Performance Standards: Query Bounding
docs.text:
The results page is complex but stays fast because of a strict "Query Bounding" rule verified in gtm/tests.py.

# gtm/tests.py
def test_results_performance(self):
    with CaptureQueriesContext(connection) as ctx:
        response = self.client.get(reverse('gtm:results', args=[self.session.uuid]))
        # Guardrail: A 36-question assessment must not trigger > 30 queries
        self.assertLessEqual(len(ctx), 30)
This is achieved by Prefetching categories and tool recommendations in bulk at the start of the view request.

docs.title: Document Processing & OCR Logic
docs.text: The GTM Validator features a hybrid document processing engine in dashboard/document_processors.py that handles the extraction of context for the AI Agent.

docs.title: 1. Hybrid PDF Extraction
docs.text: The system uses a "Chain of Extraction" pattern for PDF documents: 1. Local Parsing: Attempts to extract text using the pypdf library (fast, local). 2. AI Fallback: If local parsing fails or returns empty text, the system sends the PDF bytes to Gemini-2.5-Flash with an extraction prompt. This effectively uses the LLM as a sophisticated OCR engine for complex or scanned PDFs.

docs.title: 2. Vision-Based Image OCR
docs.text: Image attachments (screenshots of landing pages, ads, etc.) are processed using Gemini's vision capabilities. - Context Preservation: The prompt explicitly instructs the AI to preserve headings and bullet points to maintain the structural meaning of the marketing asset. - Token Optimization: To prevent token overflow, only the first 6,000 characters of extracted text are kept for context, with a further 600-character excerpt used for quick-reference history.

docs.title: 3. Attachment Processing Constraints
docs.text: The engine enforces several safety and performance limits: - Max Files: 4 attachments per message. - Max Size: 6 MB per file. - Allowed Types: A whitelist of text (.md, .json, .yaml), document (.pdf), and image (.png, .jpg, .webp) formats.

docs.title: 4. Lexical Context Selection
docs.text: When the AI Agent needs to reference an attachment in a follow-up question, it uses a lexical scoring engine (_select_relevant_attachment_sections): - It tokenizes the user's query and the available attachment excerpts. - It calculates an "overlap score" to identify which specific document or section contains the answer. - This ensures the most relevant context is prioritized within the LLM's 5,000-character context window.

docs.title: Maintenance & Operational Tools
docs.text: The GTM Validator project includes several custom management commands in gtm/management/commands/ that encapsulate critical "tribal knowledge" for system maintenance and initialization.

docs.title: 1. Framework Initialization (load_gtm_defaults)
docs.text: This is the most critical command for setting up a new environment. - The Data Structure: It contains a massive hardcoded dictionary of Categories (Demand, Conversion, Delivery), Questions (D1-D12, C1-C12, etc.), and Recommendation Bands. - Logic: It uses get_or_create to ensure the diagnostic framework is present in the database without duplicating existing data. It also populates the ai_metadata field which is essential for Gemini's reasoning.

docs.title: 2. Recommendation Seeding (load_tool_recommendations)
docs.text: This command seeds the "Software Matchmaking" engine. - Keyword Matching: It maps specific GTM keywords (e.g., "CRM", "SEO", "Attribution") to recommended software tools and descriptions. - Categorization: Every recommendation is linked to a Category (e.g., HubSpot linked to "Demand" and "Conversion").

docs.title: backfill_owners
docs.text: A legacy maintenance tool used during the transition from a purely anonymous session model to a workspace-aware model. - Logic: It identifies AssessmentSession records without an explicit user or workspace and attempts to map them based on the owner_client_id cookie history.

docs.title: 4. Asynchronous AI Monitoring
docs.text: While not a standalone command, the utils_ai_monitoring.py (if available) provides the backend for tracking AI usage across these operations. - Usage Tracking: Every call to Gemini (from a view or a command) is logged with token counts to AIUsageTracker. - Quota Guard: This data informs the _quota_cooldown_active logic to prevent exceeding Vertex AI API limits during batch operations.

docs.title: GTM Validator: A Simple Guide
docs.text: If you’re not a programmer, this page is for you. This is a plain-English explanation of what this platform does and how it helps a business grow.

docs.title: 🩺 The "Business Health Checkup"
docs.text: Imagine going to a doctor for a checkup. The GTM Validator does the same thing for your business's Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy—which is just a fancy way of saying "how you find, win, and keep customers."

docs.title: 1. The Diagnosis (The Assessment)
docs.text:
The platform asks you a series of questions about your business. - Demand: Are you finding enough of the right people? - Conversion: Are you good at turning those people into paying customers? - Delivery: Do your customers actually get what they paid for?

How the code helps: It remembers your answers and uses a "weighted" system (like a school grade) to figure out which areas are most critical for you to fix first.

docs.title: 2. The Smart Consultant (The AI)
docs.text:
Once you finish the questions, a "Smart Consultant" (powered by Google's AI) reads everything you wrote. It then writes a 30-Day Playbook specifically for you. - It doesn't give generic advice. It looks at your specific industry and your specific problems. - It even calculates how much money you might be leaving on the table and what you should do in the next month to fix it.

How the code helps: It "talks" to the AI, sends it your business details, and makes sure the advice it gives back is saved safely in your account.

docs.title: 3. The "Trust but Verify" Tool (Evidence Audit)
docs.text:
Sometimes, business owners think they are doing great, but the reality is different. You can upload things like a screenshot of your website or your sales presentation. - The AI "looks" at these files and gives you a second opinion. - If your website is confusing, the AI will tell you, and it might even lower your "Health Score" until you fix it.

How the code helps: It uses "Computer Vision" to see your images and read your PDFs, just like a human would, but much faster.

docs.title: 4. The Virtual Office (Workspaces)
docs.text:
You don't have to do this alone. You can invite your team into a "Workspace." - Everyone can see the same score. - You can turn the AI's advice into a To-Do List (Action Items). - You can assign tasks to people, set deadlines, and leave comments for each other.

How the code helps: It keeps everyone’s data separate and secure, making sure Team A can’t see Team B’s private business plans.

docs.title: 5. The Gap Tracker (Analytics)
docs.text:
The platform helps you track the "Gap" between where you are and where you want to be. - If you want 50 new customers a month but only have 10, the dashboard shows you that "Gap." - It then gives you specific tips on how to close that gap.

How the code helps: It does all the math behind the scenes to show you simple charts and progress bars so you don't have to use a spreadsheet.

docs.title: 🚀 In Short...
docs.text: The GTM Validator is a tool that diagnoses your business problems, writes a plan to fix them using AI, and gives your team a workspace to get the work done.

docs.title: Python Module Directory: Logic & Code Snippets
docs.text: This comprehensive directory provides a file-by-file breakdown of the GTM Validator codebase. It explains the core logic of every important module and includes actual code snippets to illustrate the implementation.

docs.title: 📂 gtm/ (Core Assessment Engine)
docs.text: The gtm app is the heart of the platform, managing the diagnostic framework, scoring math, and AI strategy generation.

docs.title: 📄 gtm/models.py
docs.text: Responsibility: Defines the relational schema for the assessment framework. - Category & Question: The building blocks of the diagnostic. - AssessmentSession: Tracks a single user's journey. - ResultSnapshot: A denormalized record that "freezes" the company's state and stores the final AI playbook. - GTMFile: Multimodal "Strategic Evidence" with AI audit fields.

docs.title: 📄 gtm/services.py
docs.text:
Responsibility: The "Brain" of the assessment. Contains the mathematical engine for scoring. - Logic Snippet: Weighted Scoring 

def _compute_scores(session):
    # Category-level weighted averages calculated in a single efficient query
    category_results = (
        Response.objects.filter(session=session)
        .values('question__category_id')
        .annotate(
            total_weighted_score=Sum(F('score') * F('question__weight')),
            total_weight=Sum('question__weight')
        )
    )
    # Final overall score normalized to a 100-point scale
    overall += (avg / 5.0) * (weight / total_w) * 100.0

docs.title: 📄 gtm/ai_services.py
docs.text:
Responsibility: Orchestrates interactions with Vertex AI (Gemini). Handles prompt building and response "rescuing." - Logic Snippet: Content Rescuing 

# If JSON parsing fails, we manually "rescue" the content using regex
match = re.search(r'["\']markdown_playbook["\']\s*:\s*["\'](.*?)(?=["\'],\s*["\']|["\'],?\s*\}|$)', text, re.DOTALL)
if match:
    final_playbook_text = match.group(1).replace('\\n', '\n').replace('\\"', '"')

docs.title: 📄 gtm/ai_auditor.py
docs.text:
Responsibility: Multimodal vision auditing. - Logic Snippet: Vision-to-Scoring Bridge 

# Extract "Evidence Score: 8/10" from LLM prose and map to a modifier
match = re.search(r"evidence\s+score[:\s*]+(\d+)", audit_text, re.I)
if match:
    score = float(match.group(1))
    # 1-3 -> -3 modifier, 7-10 -> +3 modifier
    return _map_score_to_modifier(score)

Responsibility: Manages the high-interactivity assessment wizard using HTMX. - Logic Snippet: Partial Rendering

Responsibility: Calculates dashboard context, trends, and task velocity. - Logic Snippet: Action Item Velocity

total_seconds = sum((item.completed_at - item.created_at).total_seconds() for item in completed_items_qs)
velocity_days = round(avg_seconds / 86400, 1)

docs.title: 📄 dashboard/document_processors.py

docs.title: Scoring & Analytics Logic
docs.text: The GTM Validator uses a two-tier weighted scoring algorithm to determine business maturity. This logic is derived from gtm/services.py and dashboard/analytics.py.

docs.title: 1. Weighted Scoring Algorithm
docs.text: The final GTM score is calculated through a hierarchy of weights:

docs.title: Tier 1: Per-Question Weighted Average
docs.text: Each response is multiplied by its question's weight. The category score is the sum of these weighted scores divided by the sum of weights. $$\text{Category Avg} = \frac{\sum (\text{Response Score} \times \text{Question Weight})}{\sum \text{Question Weight}}$$

docs.title: Tier 2: Categorical Normalization
docs.text: Categories have their own weights (e.g., Demand: 0.4, Conversion: 0.4, Delivery: 0.2). These are normalized against the total of all category weights to ensure a final score between 0 and 100. $$\text{Overall Score} = \sum \left( \frac{\text{Category Avg}}{5} \times \frac{\text{Category Weight}}{\text{Total Weight}} \times 100 \right)$$

docs.title: 2. Performance-First Results View
docs.text: The system is architected to handle large datasets efficiently: - Query Bounding: The results view is performance-tested to stay under 30 queries for a standard assessment. - Denormalization: Analytical results are cached in the ResultSnapshot model to avoid recalculating complex weighted averages on every page load.

docs.title: 3. Advanced KPI Analytics
docs.text: The dashboard calculates several non-obvious metrics to track team productivity:

docs.title: Action Item Velocity
docs.text: Measures the efficiency of the GTM team by calculating the average days between a task's creation and its "Done" status change: $$\text{Velocity} = \text{Avg}(\text{completed_at} - \text{created_at})$$

docs.title: Comparative Weekly Trends
docs.text: The system identifies "meaningful change" by comparing this week's metrics against the previous week. - Sentiment Logic: For "Pending Items", a decrease is flagged as a positive trend (pending_change_positive=True). - Activity Mapping: A 7-day time-series tracks Sessions, Tasks Created, and Tasks Completed to visualize momentum.

docs.title: 4. Gap Analysis Display Logic
docs.text: The Gap Analysis system (calculate_gap_metric_display_properties) maps numeric deltas to visual statuses: - Critical Gaps: Gaps > 50% of the target are flagged as high priority. - Categorical Sorting: Insights are sorted by both priority and category (Lead Gen, Sales Velocity, etc.) to ensure a balanced improvement roadmap.

docs.title: GTM Validator: High-Context System Design
docs.text: This document maps the business goals of the platform to the technical implementation. It provides the "Substance" for how each part of the codebase enables the project's vision.

docs.title: 1. The "Resilient Consultant" Architecture
docs.text: The core challenge of the GTM Validator is providing always-on strategic advice while relying on external AI APIs that can be slow or unavailable.

docs.title: Goal: Zero-Downtime Strategy
docs.text: Even if Google's Gemini API is down, the user must receive value. - Implementation: gtm/ai_services.py uses a Static-Fallback Pattern. - Context: If ResourceExhausted is caught, the system sets a cache-based "Quota Cooldown" and serves high-quality, pre-written advice from the RecommendationBand model.

docs.title: 2. The "Modern Monolith" UI Strategy
docs.text: We avoided the complexity of a separate React/Vue frontend to keep the AI-to-UI feedback loop as tight as possible.

docs.title: Goal: Single-Page Experience without JS Overhead
docs.text: The assessment wizard must feel like a modern app but remain fast and SEO-friendly. - Implementation: gtm/views.py uses HTMX with the HX-Request header check. - Context: The view detects if it's an partial update and returns only the form segment, saving bandwidth and improving perceived performance.

docs.title: 3. The "Snapshot" Integrity Model
docs.text: GTM strategy changes quarterly. A report from January should not change if the diagnostic questions are updated in March.

docs.title: Goal: Strategic Immutability
docs.text: Ensure that historical reports are preserved exactly as they were generated. - Implementation: gtm/models.py defines the ResultSnapshot record. - Context: Instead of linking to current Question objects, the snapshot stores a JSON-denormalized copy of all weighted scores and AI text at the time of completion.

docs.title: 4. Multi-Tenant "Soft" Isolation
docs.text: The platform needs to support team collaboration while allowing individual users to have private assessments.

docs.title: Goal: Secure but Collaborative
docs.text:
• Implementation: The safe_get_session_or_403 service in gtm/services.py.
  • Context: This function implements a hierarchical check: (1) Does the user own it? (2) If not, is the user a member of the Workspace that owns it? (3) Is their role high enough? This centralizes security logic in one place.

docs.title: 5. Token-Aware Analytics
docs.text: AI cost management is critical for a SaaS product.

docs.title: Goal: Cost Transparency
docs.text:
• Implementation: gtm/utils_ai_monitoring.py.
  • Context: Every AI call logs tokens used to the AIUsageTracker. This allows administrators to see exactly which features (Playbook vs. Chat) are driving costs and set proactive rate limits.

docs.title: Collaborative Workspaces & RBAC
docs.text: The GTM Validator implements a multi-tenant workspace architecture designed for team collaboration, as seen in gtm/models_workspace.py and gtm/views_workspace.py.

docs.title: 1. Soft Isolation Pattern
docs.text: Rather than a strict hard-tenant database split, the project uses a "Soft Isolation" pattern: - AssessmentSession Ownership: Sessions can be owned by a User (private) or a Workspace (team-shared). - Context Filtering: The get_dashboard_context utility in dashboard/analytics.py dynamically builds query filters based on the current_workspace. If a workspace is active, all private user data is automatically excluded from the analytical views.

docs.title: 2. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
docs.text:
The system defines a granular permission set through the WorkspaceMembership model:

Role Internal Permission Logic admin Full CRUD on workspace settings, members, and all assessments. manager Can start assessments and create/assign ActionItem tasks. contributor Can edit assessments and update assigned tasks. viewer Read-only access to snapshots and analytics. funti3r_consultant Specialized external role with audit-specific visibility.

docs.title: 3. Centralized Authorization (safe_get_session_or_403)
docs.text: The project avoids duplicating permission checks in views by centralizing them in gtm.services.safe_get_session_or_403. - The Protocol: 1. Fetch the session via UUID. 2. Check if session.user == request.user. 3. If not, check if session.workspace exists and if the request.user has an active WorkspaceMembership there. 4. Log any unauthorized access attempts with detailed metadata for security auditing.

docs.title: 4. Invitation Lifecycle
docs.text: Collaborative growth is managed via token-based invitations: - Token Generation: uuid4 tokens are used to create unique invitation links. - Expiration: Invitations are checked against timezone.now() to ensure they are accepted within the allowed window (typically 7 days). - Claiming: Upon acceptance, the system automatically creates the WorkspaceMembership record and transfers any pending tasks to the new user's profile.

docs.title: 5. Shared Resource Auditing
docs.text: In a workspace context, the AI Auditor (gtm/ai_auditor.py) can audit shared resources (dashboard.Resource). - Mechanism: The audit critique is stored at the workspace level, creating a shared "Strategic Knowledge Base" where all team members can see the AI's feedback on company assets.
